newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says has nothing to add to G7 statement.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says has nothing to add to G7 statement.

text.p: The German Bundesbank sees no substance in a report from U.S. news agency MNSI, quoting sources close to the German Finance Ministry, that said Germany is seeking a higher dollar.

"We can see no substance to this report," a Bundesbank spokesman said in answer to Reuter enquiries. "The Bundesbank, like the Finance Ministry, has nothing to add to the G7 statement made in Berlin," he added.

The report by Market News Service said sources close to the German finance ministry and central bank had said a further dollar rise to a range of 1.70 to 1.75 marks over time would be welcomed. It did not name the sources.

The Group of Seven (G7) meeting finance ministers and central bank governors of the world's leading industrialised nations in Berlin last Saturday issued a statement saying that while they favoured a strong dollar, the U.S. currency had now risen far enough.
A Bundesbank spokesman said that statement was made when the dollar was trading at around 1.65 marks.
